note: Explicit, user-authorized overrides for resolve_migration_citations.py. The resolver fails closed on any condition NOT covered here; these two narrow exceptions were authorized by the user during the RLCR loop and are recorded for audit.

allow_overlap_disambiguation.rule: best-fit: prefer a chunk whose page span fully contains the cited page_range, then the tightest span, then the lowest chunk_id
allow_overlap_disambiguation.scope: ONLY a multi-candidate whose matching chunks form a single overlapping page-span chain (kb's chunker emits overlapping chunks, so a quote verbatim-verifies against more than one adjacent chunk). A multi-candidate that is NOT a pure overlap chain (genuine duplicate text in distant chunks) still fails closed.
allow_overlap_disambiguation.audit: the chosen chunk_id and ALL candidate chunk_ids are recorded on the bind-report row.
allow_overlap_disambiguation.rationale: binding to the best-fit overlapping chunk is safe (the quote is a verbatim substring of the chosen chunk and its chunk_hash is correct); overlap is a structural chunker property, not content ambiguity.

allow_low_auto_bind_for_ufffe_repair.scope: the >=95% per-set auto-bind guard is overridden ONLY because some authored quotes span a Pdfium STX->U+FFFE hyphenation marker the kernel preserves; the override covers ONLY trim/re-anchor repairs whose recorded reason is that U+FFFE condition. Any unbound, zero-match, boundary-spanning, or non-overlap-ambiguous citation still fails closed.
allow_low_auto_bind_for_ufffe_repair.audit: every repair is recorded in migration_quote_audit.json; the bind report records the per-set auto-bind rates and that the override was applied.
allow_low_auto_bind_for_ufffe_repair.rationale: user hybrid decision (trim where the clean run retains >=60%, else re-anchor to the best-overlap clean on-page sentence).
